# `nish:secret`

The `nish:secret` builtin module: the globals of the same names, importable. Its members are declared in `runtime/nish.d.ts`; [the language reference](language.md#builtin-modules-nish) is the normative list.

```ts
import {
  Secret,
  expose,
  exposeWith,
  secret,
  wipe,
} from "nish:secret";
```

<scalar-card title="expose" icon="phosphor/regular/function" href="#expose">

`f(value)`.

</scalar-card>

Key material: an array of integers or a record of integer fields, held opaque.

## expose

`f(value)`. `f` reaches no I/O and no C, keeps nothing of `value`, and
declares a return type that holds no `Secret`: that type is what leaves.

```ts
function expose<T, R>(
  s: Secret<T>,
  f: (value: T) => R,
): R
```

#### Parameters

<scalar-field name="s" type="Secret&lt;T&gt;" required>
</scalar-field>

<scalar-field name="f" type="(value: T) =&gt; R" required>
</scalar-field>

## exposeWith

`f(value, arg)`, under `expose`'s rules; `f` may not write `arg` either.

```ts
function exposeWith<T, A, R>(
  s: Secret<T>,
  arg: A,
  f: (value: T, arg: A) => R,
): R
```

## secret

`value`, wrapped. A local handed in is moved: it may not be read again.

```ts
function secret<T>(value: T): Secret<T>
```

#### Parameters

<scalar-field name="value" type="T" required>
</scalar-field>

#### Returns

<scalar-field name="returns" type="Secret&lt;T&gt;">
</scalar-field>

## wipe

Zero the value's whole storage, with a store the optimiser may not remove.

```ts
function wipe<T>(target: Secret<T>): void
```

#### Parameters

<scalar-field name="target" type="Secret&lt;T&gt;" required>
</scalar-field>

Zero an array or record of integers that `expose`'s function holds, likewise.

```ts
function wipe(target: object): void
```

#### Parameters

<scalar-field name="target" type="object" required>
</scalar-field>

## Secret

Key material: an array of integers or a record of integer fields, held
opaque. Made by `secret`, read only through `expose`, and wiped or
returned by the function that made it.

```ts
class Secret<T>
```
